questions.q: What does the word ikigai roughly translate to?
a: A purpose that gives you a reason to rise
A season for rest and reflection
A craft passed down through families
A ritual for honoring ancestors
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that iki means life and gai means value, giving a reason to live.

questions.q: Which four questions does the summary suggest for finding your ikigai?
a: Strengths, the world's needs, passions and earning a living
Wealth, status, family duty and community service
Talent, luck, discipline and long-term planning
Health, friendship, travel and spiritual practice
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists your strengths, what the world needs, your passions and what you can earn a living doing.

questions.q: Why does the summary suggest you should never retire?
a: Retirement is linked to a higher risk of health problems
Retired people tend to spend too much money
Retirement removes the structure your day needs
Retired people lose contact with their families
questions.why: Lesson 1 says retirement is associated with more health problems, while purpose keeps people active.

questions.q: What advice from Okinawan centenarians does the summary highlight?
a: Worry less and enjoy what you already have
Save aggressively for unexpected medical costs
Exercise intensely for at least an hour daily
Live alone so you can follow your own routine
questions.why: Lesson 2 says centenarians worry as little as possible and focus on enjoying life.

questions.q: What kind of movement do Okinawans favor for long life?
a: Small, simple activity spread through the day
Short bursts of high-intensity training
Long runs three times a week
Daily weightlifting at a gym
questions.why: Lesson 3 says intensity can hurt consistency, so they choose easy movement like walking or radio exercises.
